correctness_argument:
A promoter is an edit to the total genomic content of the cell, so it belongs on the genotype; two releases blocked because no leaf holds one, and because their readouts would have to be stored as something they are not (#991, #990).

Genotype. PromoterReplacementPerturbation asserts that a host gene's NATIVE promoter was removed and a characterized part put in its place (SO:1000032 delins), and its required gene_namespace plus bacterial locus-tag validator refuse YKR097W. Neither release replaces a native promoter: Zhang 2020 re-integrates five genes at EasyClone sites, each arriving with one of six promoters, and Vaishnav 2022 adds a reporter whose promoter carries a variable 80 bp insert on a CEN plasmid. Both are therefore gene ADDITIONS (state present, SO:0000667 insertion) and both are new leaves under GeneAdditionPerturbation. They are two leaves, not one, because the promoter means a different thing in each: a named characterized part whose sequence the release need not deposit (promoter_sequence optional, integration_locus required), against a sequence that IS the measured independent variable (promoter_sequence required, with the 1-based span of the variable region, and no integration locus because the construct is episomal). Adding a promoter field to GeneAdditionPerturbation instead would change the meaning of a class in the closure of the served metabolite, morphology and product-titer loaders, which rule 3 reserves for owner sign-off, and would be null on every one of those records.

Readout, #991. The served PromoterActivityPhenotype cannot hold a pooled sort-seq estimate without loosening well_id, which is that class's identity rule: an arrayed reporter library holds one promoter in several wells, so without the well two readings of one promoter in one condition collapse into a single L1 identity. A pooled library has no well at all, and its identity key is the source's own sequence id. By rule 6 the physical measurement also differs: the four existing ReporterReadout members each return a reading per well or per cell, while a sort-seq number is a read-weighted average of bin indices for one sequence out of millions, so the member sort_seq_fluorescence names it and the leaf is a sibling under Phenotype rather than a tag on the served class.

Readout, #990. Zhang 2020's GFP is a trpR-based biosensor reporting intracellular tryptophan, not transcription from the five varied promoters, so PromoterActivityPhenotype would name the wrong measured entity. MeasurementType.biosensor_readout exists but lives on EnvironmentResponsePhenotype, whose verifier requires an environmental edit on every record, and a biosensor strain grown in one medium has none. MetabolitePhenotype holds a metabolite QUANTITY, so storing a fluorescence synthesis rate there would promote a proxy signal to a concentration. BiosensorFluorescencePhenotype keeps the signal in its own units and names the sensed metabolite as a typed Compound, the one class the environment and phenotype lanes already share, so the record joins the compound layer without claiming to be a titer; a release that publishes a calibration converts explicitly.

Every symbol is new or gains a member: 0 breaking, 108 datasets stale through the GenePerturbationType / ExperimentType / PhenotypeType unions and the ReporterReadout enum, which the KG 4.0 full rebuild remakes.

source_quotes.value: the released number is a read-weighted average over sort bins, which is why it is not a per-well or per-cell reading

source_quotes.note: Fixes expression_units and read_count: the observations the estimate averages are reads.

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Add promoter_name / promoter_sequence fields to the served GeneAdditionPerturbation.
alternatives_rejected.why_rejected: A field added there is in the closure of served loaders (Ozaydin 2013, Cachera 2023, Lopez 2024, Xue 2025) and would change what that class's records assert about an addition whose promoter is unknown: null would mean both 'not released' and 'native context'. Rule 3 sends a meaning change on a served class to the owner; a new leaf moves no served class.

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Make PromoterActivityPhenotype.well_id optional so a pooled library can use the served class.
alternatives_rejected.why_rejected: well_id is that class's L1 identity rule, not a convenience: Mohiuddin 2022 relies on it to keep two wells of one promoter distinct. Loosening it is field_required_loosened on a served class for a source that has no well at all.

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Widen PromoterReplacementPerturbation's gene_namespace and name validator to admit yeast systematic names.
alternatives_rejected.why_rejected: It would make every yeast record assert a native-promoter delins that neither release performed, and the widened validator would admit a bacterial locus tag into a yeast genotype. The leaf's own docstring already records that widening the base moves served CRISPR closures.

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Store Zhang 2020's biosensor signal as a MetabolitePhenotype tryptophan value.
alternatives_rejected.why_rejected: The release carries a fluorescence synthesis rate in MFI/h, not a concentration, and publishes no calibration in the loaded files; storing it as a metabolite quantity would assert a titer that was never measured. Rule 6 case 3: different physical measurement, separate leaf plus an explicit converter.

alternatives_rejected.alternative: Store the pooled sort-seq estimate under flow_cytometry_fluorescence.
alternatives_rejected.why_rejected: That member means a per-cell distribution the source summarized. A sort-seq estimate for one sequence is an average over the bins its reads fell in, often a single read from a single cell, so the member would claim a sample unit the number does not have.
